show: A History of the World in 100 Objects
titel: From The World to America: Neil MacGregor meets Roman Mars

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Roman Mars and Neil MacGregor discuss telling history through everyday objects.
kurzfassung: Roman Mars talks with the creator of the original BBC series, Neil MacGregor, about the philosophy and challenges of telling world history through physical artifacts. They explore how everyday items provide a voice for ordinary people and how this approach inspires a new US-focused companion series. The episode also previews stories and objects from the upcoming project, highlighting the hidden histories behind mundane things.
stichpunkte: Neil MacGregor reflects on launching the original BBC series in 2010 with 100 objects from the British Museum
Curators paired unrelated artifacts from different cultures to highlight common human experiences and behaviors
Choosing items chronologically revealed the growing connectedness of the world and accelerating dependencies on technology
Radio storytelling forces listeners to imagine objects, creating a deeper personal connection than seeing a static image
The project aimed to give a voice to the voiceless by focusing on everyday makers rather than rulers and written records
Roman Mars and Neil MacGregor discuss the conceptual approach behind the new spinoff series about United States history
Standardized items like the 60-degree threaded screw demonstrate how mundane objects can drive massive industrial shifts

kapitel.titel: Creating A History of the World in 100 Objects
The Radio Medium and Imagining Objects
Chronology, Global Connections, and Maker Perspectives
Choosing the Final Object and the Legacy of the Series
Advice for a U.S. Spinoff and Preview

clips.hook: Museum curators don't pound tables, but they do sulk when their items get cut.
clips.text: Museum experts did not engage in aggressive shouting matches during selection meetings, though they did passionately advocate for their preferred items and acted grumpy when pieces were rejected.

clips.hook: The Rosetta Stone started out as an intensely boring tax document.
clips.text: Ein geschichtsträchtiger Artefakt wurde ursprünglich als rein bürokratische Steuerverfügung in drei Sprachen angefertigt, ohne dass die Ersteller dessen spätere kulturelle Bedeutung ahnten.

clips.hook: Simple stone hand axes allowed humans to spread across the world.
clips.text: Frühzeitliche Werkzeuge ermöglichten es der Menschheit erst, sich global anzusiedeln, schufen gleichzeitig aber auch eine dauerhafte technologische Abhängigkeit.

clips.hook: Solar power broke the political control over electricity in remote regions.
clips.text: Unabhängige Solarenergie bricht in bestimmten Teilen der Welt den politischen Monopolanspruch lokaler Machthaber über Stromkabel und Energieversorgung.

clips.hook: Almost any screw could tell the story of American industrial dominance.
clips.text: Anhand einer standardisierten Schraube lässt sich nachzeichnen, wie die Vereinigten Staaten Großbritannien als weltweite industrielle und wirtschaftliche Supermacht ablösten.

beschreibung: In 2010, A History of the World in 100 Objects, hosted by Neil MacGregor, premiered on BBC Radio 4 to great acclaim. It was a groundbreaking series that told a complex and interconnected history of the world through 100 objects housed in the British Museum collection. Now, as America marks the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, BBC Studios is partnering with 99% Invisible’s Roman Mars to reimagine the landmark series for the United States— A History of the U.S. in 100 Objects. In this special episode, Roman sits down with Neil MacGregor to talk about how the original series came together and how to curate a collection of American objects.
untertitel: Roman Mars & Neil MacGregor on the new US spinoff: A History of the U.S. in 100 Objects.
